skills.title: Assess before deleting
skills.description: Remove a file, branch, worktree, record or process only after each candidate has been classified by what depends on it and what would be lost, and the reversible step has been taken first.
inputs: the candidates for removal, each named by its path, ref, record id or process id
a checkout with git history, the peer board and the repository's own diagnostics
outputs: a removal table naming each candidate, its class, the evidence behind the class, its risk and the action taken
a rescue ref or pushed branch for anything that held work not reachable elsewhere
the verification that ran after the removal, with its exit codes

examples.title: Remove worktrees that look finished
examples.body:
The disk is filling and several linked worktrees belong to branches that were merged. Each
one is a candidate, not a decision: a merged branch can still hold uncommitted work.

```text
Apply the assess-before-deleting skill to every linked worktree whose branch is merged into
master. Classify each with git status, the unpushed commits and the peer board; push or
rescue anything that holds work, remove only the low-risk ones, then run majordomus doctor.
```

skills.title: Deploy the site by hand
skills.description: Publish the website to GitHub Pages from a terminal, through the one script the Pages workflow runs, when waiting for the Actions queue is not acceptable.
inputs: the commit to publish, checked out with a clean tree and contained in origin/master
zola, node_modules (npm ci) and, for the full gate, cargo
the operator's word, in this session, that the site is to go live now
outputs: a gh-pages commit naming the source commit, or a refusal naming the gate that stopped it
a checkpoint recording the deploy and the commit it published

skills.title: Implement a change
skills.description: Carry a requested change through the repository evidence-first, from the invariant it must keep to a verified, reconciled, documented and committed tree, without widening its scope.
inputs: the requested change, in the requester's words, with any issue or specification it names
a checkout with git history and the effective context for every path the change will touch
the repository's verification, generation and drift-check commands
outputs: the change, as coherent commits whose messages name what each proves
behavioural evidence that distinguishes the new behaviour from the old
regenerated projections and a clean drift check
an implementation record naming the invariant, the evidence, what was reconciled and what remains unsupported

examples.title: Add a declarative catalogue item
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to add a use case under .ai/repo/use-cases/. Touch canonical
data only; then validate, regenerate, and prove that the command line, MCP and the site
show the new item with no code or registry edited; finish with the drift checks.
```

Expected shape: modify canonical data only → validate → regenerate → prove propagation
through every surface → drift check clean.

examples.title: Fix a defect
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to the defect "finish accepts a completed outcome while an
open question names the task". Reproduce it with a case under test/cases/ that fails
today, make the smallest fix, show the case passing, and review the adjacent gates for
the same shape of hole.
```

Expected shape: reproduce → regression evidence → smallest fix → the original failure
no longer occurs → adjacent regression surface reviewed.

examples.title: Implement a feature from an issue
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to issue I0042 (majordomus plan show I0042).
Scope: the paths the issue declares. Before the mechanism: the invariant, the observable
behaviour and the test that proves it. After: generate, generate-site-data, both --check,
doctor; then plan evidence and plan done with the case that proves each criterion.
```

Expected shape: inspect → invariant → observable behaviour → behavioural test →
implementation → diagnostics and documentation → verify → commit → report.

examples.title: Make an operation faster
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to make `majordomus doctor` finish under its budget.
Record the baseline (MJ_TIMING=1 majordomus doctor, majordomus bench), find the phase
that dominates, change it, compare against the baseline, and add a regression guard only
where the contract justifies one.
```

Expected shape: baseline → bottleneck identified → change → comparison → regression
guard where justified.

examples.title: Refactor a subsystem without changing its behaviour
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to refactor lib/knowledge.sh so that discovery is one function.
First write down the observable behaviour that must be preserved and the cases that pin
it; run them before and after; prove equivalence with the same outputs byte for byte.
```

Expected shape: preserved observable behaviour stated → tests before → refactor →
tests after → equivalence shown.

skills.title: Pack the repository for an outside reviewer
skills.description: Prepare a bounded, reproducible snapshot of the tracked tree for a reviewer who cannot read the repository directly, with the local half and anything secret left out and the questions the review must answer written down.
inputs: the question the outside review must answer, and the paths it concerns
a committed tree at the revision to be reviewed
outputs: an archive of the tracked tree at a named commit, with its file list and size
a brief for the reviewer naming the commit, the scope, the questions and what was left out

examples.title: A second opinion from a model without the checkout
examples.body:
A design change should be reviewed by a model in another tool that cannot read the
repository.

```text
Apply the pack-for-review skill: commit the change, take the context profile of majordomus
archive at that commit, read the dry run for anything that must not leave, and write a brief
naming the commit, the question and what the pack leaves out.
```

skills.title: Repository review
skills.description: An evidence-driven review of the actual state of the repository, or of one change to it, before meaningful engineering work is recommended or done.
inputs: a checkout of the repository with git history available
the scope under review, or the whole repository when none is given
the effective context for every path in scope (majordomus context resolve <path>)
outputs: findings, each with severity, evidence, location, the smallest correct fix and the evidence that would prove it
the list of what was checked, including the areas where nothing was found

examples.title: Review a subsystem
examples.body:
Review one directory and the documents that describe it, whether or not anything in it
changed recently. Scope is the directory; the report names the documents it was checked
against.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to lib/knowledge.sh, lib/knowledge.awk and docs/CLI.md's
knowledge section. Question: does the documented behaviour match the implementation,
and is every documented behaviour covered by a case under test/cases/?
```

examples.title: Review an implementation against its issue
examples.body:
Review a branch against the issue it claims to complete: the acceptance criteria, the
declared paths, and the evidence the issue requires.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to branch feature/x against issue I0042
(majordomus plan show I0042). For each acceptance criterion, name the test that proves it
or report that none does. Report any file the branch touched outside the issue's paths.
```

examples.title: Review the current diff
examples.body:
Review the working tree and the staged changes against the base branch before they are
committed. Scope is the diff; everything else is read for context and not reviewed.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to the current diff against master.
Scope: the files changed in the worktree. Report FAIL findings first.
```

examples.title: Review generated files and documents for drift
examples.body:
Review whether every generated surface matches its canonical source right now, by
running the repository's own drift checks and reading what they do not cover.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to the generated surfaces: run scripts/generate-site-data
--check and majordomus generate --check, then read the documents under docs/ that
describe behaviour and compare them with the commands they describe. Report every
claim a document makes that no check or test would catch if it became false.
```

examples.title: Review the whole repository's architecture
examples.body:
Review the repository against the boundaries it declares: canonical sources, generated
projections, provider neutrality, and the rules that are enforced by a reviewer only.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to the whole repository. Concentrate on sections 3 and 5 of
the procedure: every generated artifact and the check that fails when it is stale, and
every declared boundary and the code that keeps it. List the rules that are not
machine-enforced and say for each whether the tree honours it today.
```

skills.title: Report by verification state
skills.description: Write the outcome of a piece of work as claims each marked VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED by the evidence actually observed, so a reader can tell what was proved from what was only done or intended.
inputs: the work as it stands in the tree, with its commits and anything pushed
the commands that ran during the work, with their exit codes and the relevant output
outputs: a report whose every claim carries one of VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED and the evidence for it
the gaps, each with the command or decision that would close it

examples.title: Final report of a task
examples.body:
A task is closing and its report will be read by someone deciding whether to merge.

```text
Apply the report-verification-state skill to this task's outcome. One claim per line, each
marked VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED with the command and exit code behind it; BLOCKED first,
and one line per gap saying what would close it.
```
